item.title: Client-Side Image Persistence: Storing and Retrieving Base64 Data in LocalStorage
item.description:
“Client-Side Image Persistence: Storing and Retrieving Base64 Data in LocalStorage”

How can a web application persistently store an image captured or selected on one page and seamlessly display it on another page within the same session, without relying on server-side storage or re-fetching the original asset? This scenario typically necessitates serializing the image data into a string format suitable for browser storage mechanisms like localStorage.

Methods for Serializing and Storing Images via JavaScript

Several effective strategies exist for encoding image data as Base64 strings and managing their persistence using the browser’s localStorage API.

item.title: localStorage Versus sessionStorage: Key Browser Storage Differences Explained
item.description:
“localStorage Versus sessionStorage: Key Browser Storage Differences Explained”

When working with client-side persistence in web applications, developers frequently encounter the Web Storage API, specifically localStorage and sessionStorage. While both extend the base Storage interface, their persistence lifetimes and scope create critical distinctions for data handling. How exactly do these two mechanisms differ in behavior, scope, and practical application?

Persistence Lifetime: The Core Distinction

What defines the fundamental difference in how long data remains accessible in localStorage compared to sessionStorage?
